dataset.labelled_by: Brandora team: synthetic, fictional Inkloom AI marketing content, labelled against the Inkloom AI register in backend/demo.py.
dataset.note: Development items (dev) were used while building the checks. Round 1 held-out items (heldout) were written on 22 Nov after the checks were frozen; their first-run results are kept in backend/eval/history.json, and the misses they revealed were then fixed, so they now count as development data. Round 2 held-out items (heldout2) were written on 23 Nov after those fixes were frozen and are reported exactly as they come out. Clean controls are items whose correct label is no finding.

failures.text: Cut your marketing production time by 80 per cent.
failures.detail: Expected R03 · Evidence Gap on “Cut your marketing production time by 80 per cent”
failures.why: The claim is registered as “Reduce your marketing production time by 80%”. This paraphrase changes the verb (“Cut”), which the claim matcher does not treat as the same claim. The sentence is still flagged for human review as an unmapped percentage claim, so it is not missed silently, but it counts as a miss and a false alarm.

failures.text: Cut your marketing production time by 80 per cent.
failures.detail: Engine raised REVIEW · Confirm this claim’s support on “Cut your marketing production time by 80 per cent.”
failures.why: The claim is registered as “Reduce your marketing production time by 80%”. This paraphrase changes the verb (“Cut”), which the claim matcher does not treat as the same claim. The sentence is still flagged for human review as an unmapped percentage claim, so it is not missed silently, but it counts as a miss and a false alarm.

failures.text: Wishing you the best for the festive season, from the Inkloom AI team.
failures.detail: Engine raised REVIEW · Confirm this claim’s support on “Wishing you the best for the festive season, from the Inkloom AI team.”
failures.why: “Wishing you the best” is a well-wish, not a superlative claim. Only “best regards” and “best wishes” are recognised as sign-offs. It is raised for review, not as a verdict.
Preferred-term matching covers simple inflections (leverages, leveraged) but not “leveraging”, where the final “e” is dropped.

history.note: First-run results of each held-out round, kept exactly as measured. After a round is measured, its misses may be fixed; from then on that round counts as development data and a fresh held-out round is written.

failures.problem: “Pro plan: ₹1,499/month” — plan aliases were not mapped
failures.fix: Rules can list plan aliases (Professional: “Pro”), matched as whole words

failures.problem: “Try it for a month, free” — durations in words were not parsed
failures.fix: Durations in words and in weeks or months are read and converted to days; a price's billing period is not mistaken for a trial

failures.problem: “Inkloom Ai” — a wrong capitalisation was not a listed variant
failures.fix: The approved spelling is exact: any other capitalisation of the product name is flagged

failures.problem: “80 percent” — a mapped claim was only matched with “80%”
failures.fix: Mapped claims match paraphrases: “percent”/“per cent” for “%”, “number one”/“#1” for “No. 1”, any spacing

failures.problem: “Best regards” — a sign-off was flagged as a superlative
failures.fix: “Best regards” and “best wishes” are recognised as sign-offs

method: Each item is checked by the same rule engine the product uses, against the Inkloom AI register. A finding counts as correct when its rule, outcome and location match a labelled finding; anything else is a false alarm, and an unmatched label is a miss. Precision = correct / raised; recall = correct / labelled. Citation validity checks that every shown finding names the current approved source and that the source text contains the cited value, guideline words or registered claim. Unmapped claims make no factual verdict and carry no citation, so they are excluded from citation validity.
